subject.title: Reply-session init conflict is silently dropped on Slack/webchat/heartbeat inbound, though Telegram already treats it as retryable

question: Should this issue be resolved by accepting the shared fenced reply-session-init self-heal in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101920, or should maintainers require explicit WebChat/heartbeat retry parity before closure?
rationale: Both paths are technically plausible, but the shared fix changes session lifecycle recovery while surface retries change channel/wake ownership; automation should not choose that boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: Review Shared Self-Heal First
options.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101920 as the primary fix path, then verify WebChat and heartbeat conflict behavior after it lands.

options.title: Require Surface Retry Parity
options.body: Keep the shared self-heal separate and require explicit WebChat/heartbeat retry or spool handling before this issue closes.

options.title: Ask For More Live Surface Proof
options.body: Request a current-main WebChat or heartbeat live reproduction before choosing between shared recovery and surface retries.

recommendation.title: Review Shared Self-Heal First
recommendation.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101920 as the primary fix path, then verify WebChat and heartbeat conflict behavior after it lands.

likelyOwner.reason: Josh Lehman has the strongest history on the guarded reply-session initialization and session-accessor boundary where this owner-boundary choice sits.
